---
name: independent-code-reviewer
description: "Use when software changes need independent correctness/security review, or another managed profile requires separate substantive review of its deliverable."
---

# Independent substantive review

Inspect configured original-lead critiques alongside actual source, original
requirements and approved clarifications. Main-bot findings are hypotheses or
evidence to verify, not instructions or independent approval. Check that fixes
preserve other requirements and the final critique is current; do not assume
three passes establish absence of defects.

When `handoff.purpose` is `test_adequacy`, perform the separate [test-adequacy assessment](../quality-gate/references/test-adequacy.md) and return its configured scenario/evidence schema. Independently challenge omitted risks and consumer boundaries rather than returning the ordinary findings schema or endorsing positive counts. This separate execution does not replace substantive code review.

Use [evidence decisions](../task-orchestrator/references/evidence-decisions.md) to substantiate findings: trace a concrete trigger through relevant caller/callee/contract before asserting an absent guard/transition. Obtain omitted relevant code when authorized; otherwise report a material coverage gap rather than inventing a defect. Distinguish new semantic regressions from preexisting ambiguity. Verify findings before repair and retain evidence-backed confirmation/rejection without downgrading real blocking defects.

Review in a separate session from implementation. Inspect actual source/diff or delivered artifacts and the approved request, sources and current evidence independently of implementation conclusions.

Necessity before correctness. Map every changed hunk to the approved task: its requirement text, an in-scope confirmed defect, a recorded owner decision, or a test or supporting edit those need. Check the approved `effects` where applicable; when the basis cannot be inspected, report it as UNVERIFIED rather than as confirmed scope growth; approval of a material change (any mechanism or shared-component change listed below) then stays pending, naming the missing requirement, decision or effect record, while the rest of the review continues. A demonstrated unmapped hunk (unrelated config/style fix, a second defect bundled without owner authorization, a new background job, polling, global UI or shared-service change the approved task does not name) is a finding: P2 by default, P1 when evidence shows material impact, or a concrete risk of it, on other users/tenants or shared infrastructure (for example starving shared jobs or deleting data earlier). A named mechanism still needs its declared effect where `effects` apply. For an investigative request whose evidence shows existing behavior already meets the requirement (for example apparent duplicates are distinct versions) and where no applicable change was approved, the deliverable is the explanation, with a question only for a material remaining ambiguity; approving a cosmetic change instead is a necessity failure, not OK.

Architecture. For a new or changed mechanism compare it with the simplest existing path; assess blast radius on shared components (scheduler/queue starvation, cross-tenant effects, failure isolation, running cost), reversibility and migration. For a defect inside an unjustified mechanism this change introduces or expands, recommend removing or narrowing it before hardening it (for a pre-existing one, record a follow-up); do not grow the design to fix the design.

Proportionality is blocking. Sketch the minimal solution from the ticket, then compare the diff with the ticket and that sketch using [solution design](../task-orchestrator/references/solution-design.md) and its [calibration examples](../task-orchestrator/references/solution-calibration.md). Flag each mechanism that neither the ticket/acceptance nor a category (a) risk of [solution design](../task-orchestrator/references/solution-design.md#2-triage-every-risk-only-required-risks-become-code) requires (locks, transactions, claims, retries, queues, caches, polling, new IDs/columns/migrations, optional DI dependencies, re-checks of guaranteed state), shared/cross-cutting edits, bundled unrelated changes, tests for invented risks, a consumer-side workaround for a fixable source, and infrastructure added without the owner's approval. "More robust" is not a justification without a requirement; a category (a) mechanism names its concrete counterexample. Each is P2, P1 when it changes shared infrastructure or other tenants. Hunks that apply the same confirmed root-cause fix at other entry points, or remove its compensations, belong to that defect. For each infrastructure effect, check that the cited owner decision or source names that infrastructure. A diff far beyond the sketch triggers scrutiny; the finding names the specific hunks. A proportional change gets no invented findings.

For software examine correctness, missing requirements, errors, concurrency, security, compatibility, data integrity and meaningful tests. For .NET include DI lifetimes, CancellationToken propagation, EF queries/transactions, disposal, serialization and event idempotency. For other profiles use task-orchestrator's [profile evidence](../task-orchestrator/references/profile-evidence.md) and review the artifact, claims or actual resource postconditions; code-only checks do not replace that review.

Return each finding with severity, precise file/line or artifact locator, evidence, consequence and actionable fix guidance. P0/P1/P2 block approval; P3 is advisory. State what was inspected and the limits, even when there are no findings. Name the exact commit or artifact version reviewed, or the most precise available locator. Never return a bare OK: name material checks not exercised and substitutes (mocked provider/auth, fixture, synthetic data) that limit what the evidence establishes. A review of a change you implemented or co-authored in the same session (giving review findings is not co-authoring) is a self-check: label it "self-check, not independent" and do not report approval.

Use authorized local `ase` independent-session adapters for genuine runner receipts. Fixtures and descriptors prove only their protocol/structure. Blocking findings require in-scope repair, fresh checks and new independent AC/review against changed source. Preserve persisted root/stage budgets and authorization; unresolved infrastructure or scope blockers stop automatic mutation.

# Evidence, readiness and decisions

Use relevant sections for comparisons, blockers, dependencies, actionable artifacts, semantic changes or review findings. This refines the existing workflow; it adds no universal form, new approval or mandatory service. Clear authorized work proceeds. Use the [evidence brief](../assets/evidence-brief.md) when several material facts must stay aligned; otherwise retain them in existing notes.

## 1. Establish the target and reference

Identify the actual resource and relevant environment, tenant/account and consumer. For a comparison or migration, identify the reference's role and why it is authoritative for the requested result: an applicable owner decision, contract or verified provenance. Record its locator and current version. Deployed configuration proves what is used; availability, similar names and a colleague's implementation do not prove the right business baseline.

Separate inherited behavior/settings from changes introduced by this task. Reuse compatible project conventions; avoid an override solely because an inherited value differs from a guess. Investigate a material conflict with the approved target. Escalate an unresolved owner-only choice using the existing short question format. An unconfirmed reference does not authorize changing the target or unrelated systems.

## 2. Bound the claim and prove the blocker

A blocking claim names the required outcome, affected stage/dependents, and actual observation: operation, target, safe account/access-method reference, time/version, result and inspected scope. Keep credentials and raw responses out of notes. Distinguish a known failure from an unperformed check.

"Object not found in schema S with account A" is bounded evidence. "The object does not exist" needs corresponding coverage. One denied login or failed optional adapter does not prove the application is broken or all access is impossible. Try a concrete useful authorized alternative when available; an optional integration failure does not block usable CLI/file work. Do not request new access or change permissions silently.

Continue research while a specific lead can distinguish hypotheses. Stop on sufficient evidence, no useful lead, unavailable required access, an owner-only decision or an explicit stop/limit. Record the stopping reason and remaining unknowns; exhausted inspected sources are not absence everywhere. Then proceed with a supported in-scope choice or ask one material question: checked facts, unconfirmed hypothesis, recommendation/reason and decision needed. Hold affected work and continue independent approved work. Reconcile UNKNOWN external effects rather than replaying them.

## 3. Check the readiness the obligation actually needs

These are separate observations, not an automatic promotion ladder:

| Observation | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Promised/announced | Delivery is unverified. |
| Exists/visible in metadata | The object/configuration is visible in the inspected scope. |
| Usable by intended account | The required authorized operation actually succeeds through the relevant access path. |
| Structurally complete | Required fields, interfaces and version are present. |
| Data suitable for this task | Bounded actual data/postconditions meet the task requirements. |
| Consumer behavior verified | A meaningful consumer-level check demonstrates required behavior. |

Record only the levels needed for the affected obligation, with evidence and unknowns. Installed tools are not usable sessions. Metadata is not a successful SELECT. Readable empty data is valid when the contract allows emptiness; it is not proof of representative data or correct calculations. Probe the relevant intended account/consumer within existing authority; do not broaden access or copy secrets. Once required postconditions are evidenced, proceed without a ceremonial checklist or new approval.

Bind required proof to the phase and action that can produce it. A current gate judges evidence causally attainable before its authorization; a criterion it judges must not require that same AC/review/gate approval or the later effects that approval authorizes. Independent AC/review and the current APPROVED gate remain mandatory authorization checks. If proof depends on the authorized action, retain that obligation as mandatory later work, leave its result pending, and verify it after the action before declaring the overall assignment complete.

If Publisher requires the whole-task gate, moving later proof to another stage of that same task does not remove the cycle. Scope its gated contract to source acceptance and retain the later mandatory obligations in an explicit publication/finish plan or separate delivery task. As applicable, these include actual publication, intended-consumer postconditions, matching remote/local SHA and dated closure. Source approval alone does not complete the overall assignment. Correcting this phase allocation within existing authorized scope needs no new approval; preserve every original obligation, independent verification and the gate, and never label future evidence PASS.

## 4. Separate artifact purpose, state and version

For an artifact that may be executed, handed off or used as evidence, retain:

- Purpose: discussion draft, reference/example, or intended execution/delivery.
- State: draft, prepared, applied/delivered, or independently verified, supported by actual evidence.
- Identity: path/object, content hash or meaningful version, target and relevant requirement/dependency source versions.
- Unresolved placeholders/assumptions and the current next action.

A reference CREATE script for an existing object is not a command to execute. Prepared text is not an applied resource. A filename such as final.sql is not readiness evidence. Before authorized execution or execution-ready handoff, inspect exact current bytes/version, target, required inputs and unresolved placeholders. A legitimate runtime parameter is not an unresolved placeholder. Check copied text for meaningful encoding/invisible-character corruption; do not strip whitespace or rewrite strings/identifiers blindly. Reuse authorization when its scope still applies; preparation/verification grants no external action by itself.

After a material answer or changed source, identify affected assumptions, artifact versions, acceptance checks and cached conclusions. Refresh these and their dependents, mark old versions historical/superseded, and update the current brief before the next action. Keep unaffected work valid and preserve evidence of already-applied effects; refreshing a draft does not authorize replay. Use existing intake/checkpoint/knowledge fields and source references. The brief is an optional view, not a new schema or second tracker.

## 5. Verify meaning when changing implementation

For migration, translation or optimization, identify required preserved behavior and its authority. Compare old/reference and proposed behavior using relevant examples: normal/boundary cases, null/missing values, duplicates, errors, ordering, rounding/units/time windows or permission effects as applicable. Use meaningful differential checks and the actual consumer contract. HTTP success, matching columns or one happy-path row alone do not prove equivalence.

A documented platform capability is a hypothesis about this execution path until checked. A narrowing filter needs evidence that excluded data cannot affect the required result. Separate a new regression from ambiguity already in the reference. Preserve supported behavior within scope; do not silently invent a business rule to resolve ambiguity. Hold only a material unresolved choice and its dependents, with a concise recommendation; continue independent work.

## 6. Substantiate and respond to review

Trace the current trigger through caller, boundary, callee, contract and observations; cite the first divergence/consequence. Missing code is a coverage gap to investigate, never a defect. Unknowns stay UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED.

For new software bugs use `--bugfix`. Distinguish symptom, cause and workaround. Justify the correction and new layers against the contract; preserve legitimate behavior. Use grounded consumer regressions with baseline/fault-injection evidence: helper-only green tests are insufficient. Continue useful authorized diagnostics before owner questions. See [bugfix procedure](bugfix-evidence.md) on demand.

Repair confirmed in-scope findings, rerun affected checks and fresh separate AC/review. Reject disproven findings with counterproof retained in history. Never speculate or downgrade P0/P1/P2 for approval. Preserve scope/recovery limits.

## 7. Wording and scope growth

Ambiguous wording read one way is an assumption. Declare new background, polling, global UI or shared-service changes in proposal `effects` before code ([procedure](scope-growth.md)); reviewers judge their necessity.

# Three additional passes by the original main bot

After initial implementation and meaningful executed checks, the original main
chat must reconsider the whole solution three additional times for configured
nontrivial root tasks. Do not wait for the user to request edge cases. Workers
may investigate bounded questions; their reviews do not count as main-bot passes.
Independent acceptance, substantive review and software adequacy remain separate.

## Applicability and requirement authority

New CLI tasks carry `lead_review: {version:1, required:true, additional_passes:3}`.
Programmatic creators carry the explicit policy. Saved unconfigured contracts
stay historical; never fabricate old passes or silently rewrite their policy.
The requirement applies to final root completion in every supported domain.
Children/intermediate stages keep their own checks without another root barrier.

Default uncertain complexity to nontrivial. For genuinely mechanical LOW-risk
single-stage work, `lead-review classify` needs the concrete reason and current
passing checks/source. No actions, access, unresolved discovery/requirement gaps,
required children or mixed work. Reassess changed input. Independent AC must
explicitly agree with the exemption; a cheap implementation is not triviality.
Once a substantive critique is credited, the earlier mechanical classification
is historical: it cannot bypass recorded findings or the required review depth.

Every pass reads the original request and full approved contract/proposal
history from `prepare`. Include approved owner clarifications and label explicit
supersessions. Current code, implementation summaries and generated tests cannot
redefine expectations. Assess every mandatory criterion and original/latest
request using its provided requirement hash and concrete source/check evidence.
Missing relevant facts are UNVERIFIED, not invented business policies or bugs.

## The three passes

All three inspect the complete task; their principal focuses are:

1. Requirements/business scenarios: omitted constraints, contradictions,
   unsupported assumptions and consistency with approved clarifications.
2. Attempts to break the result: boundaries, invalid inputs, dependency errors,
   repeated/concurrent effects, recovery, relevant security and performance.
   Performance conclusions need measurements. Justify inapplicable areas.
3. Whole-solution requirement reconciliation after fixes: interactions, actual
   consumer behavior, meaningful assertions and regression coverage. Check every
   original/current obligation again.

Zero findings is legitimate. A finding identifies a requirement, concrete
violation/counterexample, source and executed evidence. Investigate suspicions;
do not mutate for speculative defects, preferences or invented requirements.
Where useful, check that tests detect a relevant deliberately broken behavior;
passing counts alone do not establish fault detection.

**Record the assessment before fixes.** Repair confirmed in-scope findings under
existing authority, rerun affected checks/regressions, then perform the next
pass on current facts. If input changed before capture, retain the original
response as stale, settle its ticket and prepare a current critique. Earlier
valid passes survive later fixes, but the final critique must be current. A fix
after pass three requires a corrective follow-up. Explicitly resolve earlier
finding IDs; omitting them cannot close them.

A new approved requirement anchor starts its own three-pass depth. It does not
close old material findings, even when a criterion is renamed or removed. The
host replays authenticated prior series, including old databases without carry
fields. `prepare.finding_ledger` identifies each finding's original anchor.
New response schemas require `origin_anchor_sha256` in resolutions: use an empty
string for this series or the exact inherited origin for an older finding.
IDs may be reused in another series without conflating their obligations.
Legacy responses remain local to their original series. A `fixed` disposition
needs changed evidence; `not_a_bug` needs counterproof under the original rule
or a concrete explicit saved owner-approved supersession, challenged by AC.
Old open findings also block a later trivial exemption. Original inputs for
inherited obligations remain available beside current passes; old passes never
count toward current depth. Missing/tampered credited history blocks completion.

Three is initial checking depth, not a guarantee or a repair cap. Continue for
material gaps under existing progress-sensitive recovery. Three unsuccessful
repair cycles without verified progress trigger reassessment; another review
paragraph is not progress. Ask only for a genuine remaining decision/access/scope
blocker. Routine fixes and further supported checks do not need another approval.

## Native host and local CLI

Bind the original chat with `events bind` using actual available backend/thread/
host identity. If native identity is unavailable, use explicit `events bind-local`
and its local owner. Never invent an ID, replace the lead or start a new lead per
pass. In project-local mode use that project's installed launcher.

```text
ase lead-review status TASK
ase lead-review prepare TASK --thread-id ORIGINAL --expected-revision N
# Perform the returned critique in that same original main chat.
# Save the assessment and host-observed origin/unique native turn reference.
ase lead-review record TASK --attempt ATTEMPT --thread-id ORIGINAL --expected-revision M --file result.json
ase lead-review recover TASK
```

`prepare` commits CAS intent before native work. `record` seals the already
observed response before its SQL projection. On interruption inspect the exact
ticket, native output and saved captures through status/recover; do not resend a
prompt or start a replacement. Complete saved output recovers without a model
call; partial original bytes remain for reconciliation. Native origins are
cooperative host attestations, not independent CLI receipts or OS isolation.

Each ticket seals its prepared source hashes and complete check receipts. After
the response is captured, referenced source bodies and associated executed logs
are sealed before SQL credit. Recovery reuses the exact response and sealed
inputs. If bytes changed before they could be saved, keep the response historical
and perform a current follow-up; never label today's code as an earlier input.

Whole-root packets include verified historical bodies once by content hash. Read
each pass's `inputs` mapping in `_ase_context/lead_review.json`: `packet_path`
can name either an identical current file or `_ase_lead_history/<hash>.txt`.
Compare earlier findings with their original inputs and current corrections.
For a reference with `encoding: line_delta_v1`, `packet_path` instead names a
JSON recipe; verify that file against `representation_sha256`. Its base is a
complete current file in this same packet, identified by `base_packet_path` and
`base_sha256`. Split that base with `splitlines(keepends=True)`. In order, copy
the unchanged base lines before each `start`, append that edit's `content`, and
skip the original base lines through `until` (exclusive); append the remainder.
All indexes refer to the original base. Verify the restored UTF-8 bytes against
the reference's `sha256` and recipe's `source_sha256` before using them as old
evidence. This is read-only reconstruction, never an edit to the current project.
Recipes cannot chain; source size, line/edit counts, ordered ranges and exact
reconstruction are checked by the host. Unhelpful deltas remain raw. The durable
archives retain every original byte; a still oversized packet remains blocked.
An approved-intent `contract` may reference the complete identical
`_ase_context/contract.json` already in that packet via `$ref` and its UTF-8
SHA256. Restore that decoded object before checking original intent/approval
hashes; differing historical contracts remain complete. Stored intent and
`prepare` still supply the original complete data.
A `/scope` reference may also list `exclude_resources`: remove only those
resources in the existing order, then verify `value_sha256` of the restored
canonical JSON. This reconstructs an exact older scope; it never removes inputs
from the current task or grants authority. Different remaining fields stay full.
When identical optional-source notes are shared in coverage, that exact note
applies to every omitted-source row; all individual policies and gaps remain.
Older passes can use only an exactly bound, authenticated archived Runner request;
its original verdict remains historical and is not a new acceptance. Missing,
tampered or oversized input coverage is explicit and prevents verified completion.
Do not ask the owner to reconstruct retrievable local evidence or silently drop
an earlier finding to obtain approval. Stage packets avoid the final-root barrier.

`awaiting_lead_review` from run/resume is an internal continuation. The main bot
performs its next pass; it does not ask for approval, stop with a user blocker or
repeat successful tests/independent calls just to await itself. After current
passes, obtain final independent verification. Whole-root receipts separately
bind the lead-assessment digest; stage/action context remains reusable. These
passes never replace independent AC/review/adequacy.

For remote or non-file work, use the exact `check_sources[check_id]` returned in
the prepared base: it names the captured log (or actual check record) included in
the packet. A URL supplied by the owner is scope, not proof of observed state.
Closing a finding as fixed requires a changed source, plan, action proof or
parsed observed outcome. New timestamps from rerunning identical checks do not
establish a fix; independent acceptance still checks the actual correction.
Approved proposals are retained in full, so use credential references and never
put passwords/tokens in proposal fields or saved requirement text.

# Profile evidence

Select a profile by the requested action. A finance report's data warnings are not software debugging; changing the generating code is software. Mixed tasks map every obligation to stages and child tasks without weakening parent coverage.

Apply the [readiness proof boundary](evidence-decisions.md#3-check-the-readiness-the-obligation-actually-needs) when allocating profile evidence. Current acceptance uses proof causally attainable before its gate; later authorized effects remain mandatory in the publication/finish plan or delivery task and pending until checked. A whole-task publication gate includes all its stages, so stage reassignment alone cannot separate future proof. Phase-local source approval does not establish publication, postconditions or overall completion.

| Profile | Evidence to collect |
| --- | --- |
| software | Executed mandatory commands, positive test counts, no skipped required tests, independent AC and code review, current source/contract/plan fingerprints |
| infrastructure | Actual resource identity, before/after observations, operation intent and reconciliation, independent postcondition evidence; no invented resource success |
| document | Required artifact, readable rendering/structure where applicable, required content and traceable sources, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| research | Sources and dates, claim-to-source coverage, clear inference and uncertainty, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| mixed | Required parent coverage across all child profiles and stages; no completed parent while mandatory children remain unresolved |

Configured evaluators determine executed facts; model judgments remain separate. Manual confirmation counts only when explicitly specified as a criterion, with its source. A protocol test establishes the protocol only. Missing mandatory resources or independent execution remain BLOCKED. Local reliability records do not enforce publishing against another process with the same OS identity; trusted CI and server rules are required for that boundary.

# Test adequacy before software completion

Use for software and software stages of mixed tasks. A large passing test count establishes executed examples; judge whether those examples can catch plausible violations of the original requirements.

New software tasks created through the CLI enable `test_adequacy: {"version":1,"required":true}`. Programmatic task creators must carry that explicit policy. Preserve saved contracts and label old unconfigured adequacy honestly. A request to exclude tests from a commit/PR concerns publication; it does not remove local testing or adequacy obligations.

## Before implementation

Inspect current code, relevant existing tests, project examples and actual available test tools. Derive a concise scenario plan from original acceptance and triaged risks ([risk triage](../../task-orchestrator/references/solution-design.md#2-triage-every-risk-only-required-risks-become-code)). Only a category (a) risk - required by the ticket, an acceptance criterion or the reviewer, or needed so the change does not break existing auth, invariants or data - becomes a required scenario, code and tests; a risk existing behaviour already handles, or an unlikely/out-of-scope one, goes to `not_applicable` with its reason and to the PR's "Not handled" list. Every mandatory software criterion/stage needs a required scenario. Save it through `ase adequacy plan TASK --file plan.json --expected-revision N`.

Each scenario has `id`, `acceptance_ids`, `risk`, `boundary`, `expected`, `evidence_ids`, `required`. The plan also contains `not_applicable` rows with `risk` and a source-supported `reason`. Choose meaningful scenarios rather than an exhaustive checklist. Keep ordinary technical choices autonomous.

When a required risk applies, choose evidence that can catch it. Examples of relevant boundaries (they are not a checklist of risks to add):

| Requirement/risk | Discriminating evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Two workers must not process the same item | Real concurrent workers/connections synchronized at the competing operation; one claim/effect, including restart. Sequential calls through one stub do not exercise the race. |
| State/permissions can change during I/O | Pause at the relevant boundary, change the state, resume and observe the required externally visible result. Initially-private fixtures alone do not cover Public to Private during a read. |
| Select latest version | Equal ordering keys, duplicates, missing values and insertion orders when relevant. Distinct timestamps alone do not cover ties. |
| HTTP validation/status | Request through the actual HTTP boundary and inspect response/status/persistence. A handler exception alone does not establish what a caller receives. |
| SQL claim/transaction semantics | Actual supported database/connection behavior for the relevant transaction; an in-memory mock alone cannot establish database concurrency. |
| Retry/crash/external effect | Lost acknowledgement, known/unknown application, deduplication and recovery of the same operation. A missing observation is not nonapplication. |

Record only applicable risks. A local file operation does not need an invented HTTP test. If the approved environment cannot supply a required boundary, identify exactly which result remains unverified and seek a useful authorized alternative before asking the owner.

## Independent assessment

After actual checks, run the configured independent adequacy session in addition to ordinary AC and substantive review. It uses a separate captured execution/provider session and examines original requirements, plan, actual test source/assertions, executed logs, relevant production paths and current evidence. Implementation summaries and test names alone are locators.

When `handoff.purpose` is `test_adequacy`, return the configured adequacy schema. Evaluate each planned scenario and add relevant omitted scenarios independently. For every PASS supply current check IDs, test source, test IDs and the assertion that discriminates the failure. Report missing required boundary/source evidence as UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED; confirmed violated behavior is FAIL. A boolean adequate, a large count, source text containing a test name or a mocked success cannot substitute for actual proof. Do not claim exhaustive bug absence.

The runtime binds the assessment to the exact plan, source, contract, proposal, checks and relevant stage/context. Missing, insufficient, reused or stale assessment blocks configured completion. A passing source assessment does not establish publication or future deployment results.

The original lead handles current coverage gaps/findings without waiting for the owner to say "check edge cases". Confirm findings, repair in scope, execute affected tests and obtain fresh independent judgments. Preserve the existing progress-sensitive stop/reassessment rules; do not loop until another model says PASS. Ask only for material remaining owner decisions, unavailable required access or scope changes, with a short checked-evidence hypothesis and recommendation.

# Proportionate solution design

Use before choosing how to implement a software or infrastructure change. Build the smallest
change that meets the ticket's acceptance criteria and fits the project's existing patterns, the
way a careful developer on this team would. Correct code with unrequested machinery is a failed
delivery: the team has to remove it. A workaround that avoids touching the right code is not
"small" either. Scale the steps below to the task: one line each for a trivial change. See the
[calibration examples](solution-calibration.md).

## 0. Understand the problem first; code comes after

The first deliverable is a short problem analysis, before any code:

- **What happens now**, reproduced or traced in the code: the actual flow and data.
- **Where the system already meets the condition**: the existing point that detects or handles
  it (the place where using a token fails, the status transition, the query that selects items).
- **The smallest hook point** for the change.
- **The ticket class**: code change, investigation/clarification, or both.
- **For a defect**, its scope: every entry point with the same root cause and any earlier
  compensations for it.

For a bug, first check that the behaviour is really a defect. When it is a question of
expectations (rows that differ by version, data the reporter misread), the deliverable is a
ticket comment or question to the reporter, not code. Write no code until the analysis exists
and matches the ticket.

## 1. Understand the system before deciding

- **Business need.** Restate what the requester needs to happen, not only the wording.
- **Scoped system map** (C4, only the part the change touches): dependent apps/users;
  services/apps, how they exchange data and **who owns each contract**; components and the
  existing path for this kind of work; the files to change and their size. Use code, config,
  docs/ADRs, Git history and PR/issue discussion; mark what is unverified.
- **Reuse first.** Before adding any mechanism, search for the project's existing one
  (email/notification command, job, transaction pattern, validation, caching, auth check) and use
  it. Record what you searched and found.
- **Precedent.** Follow the team's established way unless evidence shows it no longer fits. On a
  codebase new to you or the team, match the existing code style and change size over general best
  practice, and apply this guide strictly.
- **Root cause.** For wrong or missing data, trace caller -> boundary -> callee to the first place
  the value becomes wrong.

## 2. Triage every risk; only required risks become code

For each risk scenario you can think of (race, transient failure, stale data, duplicates,
concurrent edits), classify it:

- **(a) Required** -> code and test it. A risk is required when:
  - the ticket, an acceptance criterion or the reviewer asks for it; or
  - without it, the change itself would break the project's existing authorization, validation
    or error conventions on new paths, existing invariants and contracts, lose or corrupt data,
    or duplicate external or financial effects (with a concrete counterexample).
- **(b) Already handled** by existing behaviour (a one-time state transition, an existing
  transaction, a later re-check) -> note where.
- **(c) Unlikely or out of scope** -> do not code it; list it under "Not handled" in the PR with
  the reason ("not required by AC-x; no observed trigger").

"More robust" is not a requirement. A theoretical race is (c) unless the ticket or evidence makes
it real.

## 3. Hook into existing flows; mechanisms need a reason

Prefer the place where the system already encounters the condition. Add no new scheduled job,
trigger, pipeline, polling, or global/root UI component (app shell, root component, global
layout) unless the ticket explicitly requires it.

Locks (local or distributed), new or conditional transactions, atomic claims, retries, queues,
caches, polling, version/incident IDs, new columns/tables/migrations, and optional or nullable DI
dependencies are added only when:

- a category (a) risk needs them, or
- the project already uses that exact mechanism for that exact flow.

Otherwise leave the risk documented and unhandled, or ask the owner. Do not wrap new code in
defensive re-checks of state the existing code already guarantees.

Whether an addition beyond the ticket is "really needed" is not your call. Keep it only as an
explicit question to the developer or lead, with its reason; never keep it silently.

## 4. Fix at the source, for every consumer

- Fix the component that produces the wrong value. When the confirmed root cause is in shared
  code (DB context mapping, middleware, a shared handler), fixing it there is in scope; declare it
  as an effect with its blast radius.
- Code in another repository (another team's service) is changed through its own managed task or
  child task, with its own baseline, gate, review and publication authorization. Prepare that
  change; the other team's code review is not an owner approval and does not hold your work.
- A consumer-side workaround (mapper, fallback, re-computation, retry, cache) only when the source
  is outside your access or authority (external vendor, frozen system): put it at the integration
  boundary, mark it with the upstream reference and removal condition, and tell the owner.
- After fixing a source, find other consumers of the same fault and earlier compensations; fix or
  remove them, or record why not.
- When the same fault exists at several entry points, fix every one in this change. Use a shared
  handler/mapping when one already exists for that purpose; otherwise apply the same small fix at
  each entry point and offer the shared version as a separate ticket. These hunks belong to the
  defect, not to "unrelated changes".

## 5. Choose a proportionate form

State the chosen form, why not simpler and why not more complex.

| Situation | Proportionate form | Wrong in either direction |
|---|---|---|
| A few lines in a large file | Edit those lines | Refactoring "while here" |
| Substantial new logic for a large file | New classes/files (folder, or a project in the solution when large), called from the existing code | Growing the large file further |
| The task changes most of a component's logic | Restructure that part, tests first, risk stated | Patching around it |
| The ticket says how to do it ("do not refactor") | Follow it; note any risk | Overriding the instruction |
| Data available through one simple join/navigation | Read it there | A duplicate column |
| Data required by the ticket and not stored anywhere | A new column with justification | Heuristics, log parsing, heavy procedures |
| A new entity with its own lifecycle | A new table (infrastructure, see 6) | Overloading unrelated tables |
| A monolith needs a capability | A module/project in the solution, reusing existing services | A new service, function or queue |
| Several services need a capability none provides | A dedicated component/service (infrastructure, see 6) | Copying it into each service |
| A policy value changes | Change the value and its test | Config systems, date switches, flags |

## 6. Who decides

- **You decide** (justify in the proposal): code in any number of services in this workspace, new
  files/folders/projects inside a solution, refactoring the task warrants, root-cause fixes in
  shared code, and `kind: "schema"` changes - a column, index or constraint migration a requirement
  needs - and contract changes between your services with consumers updated.
- **Incidental shared-code changes** - hardening, claim logic or other edits to job runners,
  schedulers, publishers, DB context, DI setup or middleware that the root cause does not need -
  stay out of a feature ticket. Paths listed in `.devframework/protected-paths.txt` additionally
  block the gate until `ase authorize-protected` records the owner's permission; ask for it in the
  approval format below and build no workaround meanwhile.
- **The owner approves before you build** any added or removed infrastructure (`kind:
  "infrastructure"`):
  - a service or application;
  - a database or a table;
  - an Azure Function or other serverless unit;
  - any timer, scheduler or background job, including an in-process hosted service;
  - a queue, topic or subscription (a new message type on an existing queue is code);
  - an external platform or provider;
  - a new cloud resource.

  DB functions, procedures and triggers count as infrastructure unless the project already uses
  them for that kind of logic. Declare each with basis `ASSUMPTION` on a blocking unknown; only the
  owner's answer resolves it, never a retrievable fact (`DECISION` once answered). A source ref
  counts only when the owner's own text names that infrastructure: that is pre-authorisation;
  report it afterwards. The CLI checks only the binding; reviewers check that the record names the
  infrastructure. Do not build it before approval.
- **The approval request** gives:
  - the business need and the evidence;
  - the options from simplest up (for example lazy expiry on access, an existing job, sending from
    each service), and why each is or is not enough;
  - the recommendation and its impact on other services, operations and cost;
  - one decision to make.
- **Do not ask** about what code, docs or history answer, internal design choices, which team
  reviews code, or release timing for a change you can prepare now. When the ticket implies a date
  ("from next month"), state the date you read and proceed; put it in the release note instead of
  holding the change.

## 7. Developer ownership and human-led mode

- Give a short walkthrough the developer can explain line by line: why this place, why this size,
  what was deliberately left out.
- **Human-led mode** is on only when the task explicitly asks for it, or when AGENTS.md contains the
  exact line `DevelopmentFramework mode: human-led` (then for the whole project). Nothing else
  enables it. In this mode the developer writes the production code. DF:
  - gives the analysis, hook point, step plan and test proposals;
  - writes tests only on request;
  - independently reviews the developer's diff and polishes text.

  The task runs under the research/review profile, without an implementation gate.

## 8. One ticket, proportionate tests, plain PR

- One ticket per PR. An unrelated bug found on the way goes to a note or a separate branch/PR.
- Tests cover the acceptance criteria and category (a) risks, written, not promised; prove the
  original failure through the real consumer path where practical. When no test project covers the
  changed layer, add the smallest one to the solution (your call) instead of leaving a test plan.
  No tests for invented races, and no test volume several times larger than the change.
- Required side effects (messages, payments) avoid duplicates on retry and keep related writes in
  one existing transaction where the context allows (an instance of 2(a)). Prefer a reliable signal
  over a heuristic.
- PR description: short and plain - what the ticket asked, what changed, what was deliberately not
  handled, how it was verified. No showcase of mechanisms.

Independent review checks proportionality as a blocking criterion: unrequired mechanisms,
incidental shared-code edits, bundled unrelated changes, avoidable workarounds and unapproved
infrastructure are findings. A diff far larger than the minimal sketch triggers that scrutiny; the
finding names the specific unrequired hunks.
